key_insight: Geometry-based fragmentation enables multiscale polymer representations without predefined chemical fragmentation rules.
engineering_relevance: Combining polymer sequence representations with 3D geometry can improve property prediction while highlighting structurally important regions.
method: Partition structures using radius-constrained optimization inspired by k-center clustering.
Vary the radius to control fragment size and build multiscale representations.
Fuse p-SMILES and 3D conformational information through geometric fragment-based attention.
evidence_signal: On a benchmark polymer dataset, adding 3D conformational information improved prediction accuracy for several properties over p-SMILES-only models; explainability analyses examined physical relevance.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify gains or establish robustness to conformer selection and unfamiliar polymer chemistries.
paper_title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
